payload.summary: Phase B intent PRE-CLAIM uses ttl=600 with NO heartbeat, so the intent mutex expires under a still-running agent and silently stops protecting.

evidence.release_result: both task_release calls returned ok:true released:0 — already expired
evidence.concurrent_risk: 2 peer router sessions were live in session-presence during the window; either could have claimed the freed key and spawned a second concurrent po
evidence.heartbeat_gap: the only task_heartbeat in CARD.md is line 33, on the re-entrant SAME-SESSION collision branch — it never fires periodically during a spawn, so nothing renews the lock

payload.why_it_matters: This inverts the guard: a lock intended to prevent two sessions running the same agent becomes a duplicate-ENABLER partway through every long run. po runs 15-17min routinely (two samples today: 937s, 1009s), so its gate is expired for the tail of essentially every invocation. Same shape as the already-recorded resume-key ttl=3600 inversion, but far more frequent because 600s is well under normal agent runtime.
proposed_fix_directions: raise Phase B ttl to exceed realistic agent runtime (>=3600), OR
heartbeat the intent lock from the router while the spawned agent is live, OR
release-on-return only and treat an expired-at-release (released:0) as a loud signal rather than a silent no-op
payload.negative_control: a fix must NOT make a genuinely dead sessions lock un-reclaimable; orphan reclamation via the presence/force-release ladder must still work.
